identification: SmartAssembly-protected Explorer impersonator carrying an njRAT 0.7d variant
verdict_basis: M128 is the managed entry point and checks debugger state, patches ETW, tests connectivity, then silently installs or activates the embedded payload.
M129 reconstructs the embedded PE by Base64, AES-256-CBC/PKCS7, repeating-key XOR and gzip, then calls M57/M56 with the resulting bytes and the Windows .NET Framework RegAsm executable as the host.

M56 creates a suspended process, reads its PEB, conditionally unmaps its image, allocates remote RWX memory, copies replacement PE headers/sections, replaces PEB.ImageBaseAddress and saved CONTEXT.Eax, sets the context and resumes execution.
M127 obtains ntdll's EtwEventWrite through GetProcAddress, constructs a one-byte native RET patch, changes protection with VirtualProtect and writes the patch with Marshal.Copy.

M142 reads its own executable, writes a hidden copy under AppData/Microsoft/Windows with a U+200B-spliced executable name and relaunches it without a window. M144 registers the same hidden name in HKCU's CurrentVersion/Run key.

The decoded payload's entry M96 calls OK.ko (M41). OK.RC (M48) reads framed socket input and routes it to OK.Ind (M38), whose branches execute supplied/downloaded files, load and invoke supplied assemblies, capture/send screenshots, uninstall/update, and dispatch further plugin commands.

The merged plg.A.ind implementation includes a hidden cmd.exe process with redirected stdin/stdout/stderr, process/file/registry control, TCP connection control and system commands. Shell output is sent through the response path.

OK.CheckBloggerLive (M56 in the payload) fetches one of eight rendezvous URLs, splits the response on commas, parses the first two fields as host/port and supplies the discovered endpoint to TCP connection setup. A fetched referenced configuration has the expected host,port,DIRECT,token shape. No C2 socket connection was made during analysis.

packaging.signature_interpretation: The valid strong name binds bytes to the embedded assembly key. It does not authenticate the claimed Microsoft publisher; there is no Authenticode certificate.

decoded_payload.configuration_defaults: BD, Idr, IsF and Isu are False. Do not infer active critical-process protection or the payload's optional self-install branches from capability alone.

limitations: Analysis is static. Windows code, remote tasking and downloaded executable stages were not executed. Actual deployment context, successful victim communication and the operator's identity are unavailable.

The separate M141 NtDelayExecution RET-patching routine imports GetProcAddressAPI from kernel32.dll, unlike the valid GetProcAddress import used by M127. Its exception handler permits failure; successful delay patching is not claimed.
The source has a keylog command token but this recovered stage does not establish a live keystroke recorder. No keylogging trait was invented.

The original PE is not an archive and cleave reports zero archive members. The AES-encrypted embedded PE required manual static extraction; the automatic scan does not expose that stage as an archive member.

corrections.unsupported_claims: The matcher requires API and path co-occurrence, not a payload-to-file data flow, a hidden file attribute or cmd.exe/shell execution. In this actual specimen the decrypted payload goes to RunPE; the on-disk write is a copy of the outer loader. T1059.003 was unsupported.
corrections.retention: Preserve every original matcher leg and scope as a notable Run-key/decode/launch API profile. Distinct new hostile rules require the CIL entry-point rewrite, ETW RET-patch or concealed self-copy evidence.

corrections.correction: Move build provenance to metadata/build/protector and the generic PoweredByAttribute name to metadata/binary/symbols/name/token. Preserve matchers, scope and effective criticality, and rewrite exact and ancestor consumers. The union reproduces old selector membership; JS-only consumers cannot select the moved managed rules and need no added dead alternative.

coverage_review.material_attack_losses: None. The misleading hostile profile is retained as a precisely described notable observation; three evidence-supported hostile behaviors replace its unsupported inference. SmartAssembly and PoweredBy matches retain their levels under corrected IDs.
coverage_review.other_positive_review: Searched local original samples and PE fixtures for every required API of the old profile. The only original match identified is this specimen; xworm-v3-obfuscated-client.exe is a candidate with similar APIs and retains all nine independent hostile findings. Existing SmartAssembly PE fixtures were absent; marker-preserving consumer rewrites were audited directly.
coverage_review.classifier_disagreement: The original classifier miss is closed. The manually extracted njRAT stage remains hostile with confidence 100. The engine warns that the installed v18 feature model predates feature schema v21; no classifier or engine source was modified.
